newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel minister resigns job in Netanyahu snub.
newsitem.headline: Israel minister resigns job in Netanyahu snub.

text.p: A minister in Benjamin Netanyahu's cabinet resigned on Saturday from her job as coordinator between the government and parliament in a sign of further discontent with the Israeli prime minister within his own Likud party.
Communications Minister Limor Livnat stopped short of giving up her cabinet seat but will not defend the government in parliament at a key no-confidence motion this Tuesday.
"It is difficult for me to fulfill my duties as coordinating minister because I am not a partner in the decision making procedures," Livnat said in a statement.
Livnat's move came in the wake of the resignation of Likud insider Dan Meridor as finance minister last week after he was forced out by arch-rival Netanyahu in a row over currency reform.
Former Science Minister Benny Begin, also of the Likud party, resigned the cabinet earlier in the year.
Netanyahu is further threatened with the possible rebellion of the Yisrael ba-Aliya immigrant party, which has the power to deprive the prime minister of his parliamentary majority.

The party, led by former Soviet dissident Natan Sharansky who is Minister of Industry and Trade, is upset with Netanyahu for not honouring commitments in their coalition agreement and for his delay in adopting proposals aimed at better government.

Yisrael ba-Aliya commands seven seats in the coalition's 66-seats in the 120-member parliament. If a no-confidence motion passes with a simple 61-seat majority, new elections are held for prime minister and parliament.

Analysts said there was little chance Yisrael ba-Aliya would bring down the government in Tuesday's opposition-sponsored no-confidence vote but said Netanyahu was weakened by growing disgruntlement within his party and coalition.
